requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, with pagination

guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code flows for user-owned applications. For read-only issue-title access, read_api is the documented applicable scope and covers the project issues endpoint with pagination. The connected person must still be able to access the target project, and tokens expire after two hours unless refreshed.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Use the authorization code flow with PKCE for an individual user-owned OAuth application
findings.detail: GitLab supports authorization code with PKCE, recommended for client and server apps, and authorization code. Registration in the user's account is required before the flow can start.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own GitLab account via OAuth

evidence.quote: This flow is recommended for both client and server apps.
Create a user-owned application
registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API including projects and their issues
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It is sufficient for queries and covers GET /projects/:id/issues. Narrower scopes such as read_user or read_repository do not cover issue listing, and api grants write access that is not needed.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing issue titles for projects the connected person can access

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.
Scope Description api Grants complete read/write access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, the dependency proxy, and the package registry.

findings.title: The connected person must be able to access the target project
findings.detail: The API returns issues the authenticated user can access. Private projects require credentials, and the OAuth token does not grant access beyond the connected person's own project access.
findings.appliesWhen: Target project is private or restricted

evidence.quote: If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.
List all project issues

findings.title: OAuth access tokens expire after two hours and require refresh
findings.detail: By default access tokens expire after 7200 seconds. Integrations must use the refresh_token to obtain a new token. Self-managed administrators can change token lifetime.
findings.appliesWhen: Any test or production run exceeds the token lifetime

evidence.quote: By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations that use access tokens must generate a new token with the refresh_token attribute. Refresh tokens can be used even
On GitLab Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated, administrators can configure the token lifetime. For more information, see modify OAuth access token maximum lifetime .
ruby parameters = 'client_id=APP_ID&refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN&grant_type=refresh_token&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI'

steps.title: Register a user-owned GitLab OAuth application
steps.detail: In the GitLab UI, select your avatar, Edit profile, Access > Applications, then Add new application. Enter a name and redirect URI, select read_api, and save. Copy the Application ID and Secret. Use the token endpoint at https://gitlab.com/oauth/token for GitLab.com or your own instance base URL for Self-Managed.
steps.doneWhen: Application ID and client secret are stored securely and the redirect URI matches the value used in the authorization request.

steps.title: Send the connected person through the authorization code flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Generate STATE, CODE_VERIFIER and CODE_CHALLENGE, then redirect the connected person to the authorize endpoint requesting read_api. This step is a browser redirect and is not executed by curl; it must be performed by the connected person.
steps.doneWhen: The connected person approves access and the app receives a code on the redirect URI with a matching state value.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code and the CODE_VERIFIER at the documented token endpoint. Send all required form fields. The response includes access_token and refresh_token. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, token_type, expires_in and refresh_token.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles for a project
steps.detail: Call the project issues list endpoint with the access token. Output is a JSON array of issues; read the title property from each item. Pagination requires following the next cursor or page information returned by the response.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array, each element showing a title property. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: List all project issues
Example request: shell curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
--url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/4/issues" Example response:

fields: PROJECT_ID: user-provided project ID or URL-encoded path

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using the returned cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same project issues request with the next cursor value from the prior response. Continue until the response contains no further next cursor. Do not treat one or two pages as a complete listing.
steps.doneWhen: The next cursor is absent or the documented end condition is reached, and all returned titles are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
